title: 2013 HMMT November General Problem 3
statement: A 24-hour digital clock shows times \(h: m: s\), where \(h, m\), and \(s\) are integers with \(0 \leq h \leq 23\), \(0 \leq m \leq 59\), and \(0 \leq s \leq 59\). How many times \(h: m: s\) satisfy \(h+m=s\) ?

solutions.text: 1164 We are solving \(h+m=s\) in \(0 \leq s \leq 59,0 \leq m \leq 59\), and \(0 \leq h \leq 23\). If \(s \geq 24\), each \(h\) corresponds to exactly 1 solution, so we get \(24(59-23)=24(36)\) in this case. If \(s \leq 23\), we want the number of nonnegative integer solutions to \(h+m \leq 23\), which by lattice point counting (or balls and urns) is \(\binom{23+2}{2}=(23+2)(23+1) / 2=25 \cdot 12\). Thus our total is \(12(72+25)=12(100-3)=1164\).
